retention_sensitivity.note: 'screened' is the analyzed sample (a-priori inclusion rule applied: one row per attempt slot). Two counterfactual arms are reported. 'retained_all_emitted_rows' analyzes every emitted row including superseded regenerations -- note that this DOUBLE-WEIGHTS every retried slot and its sequence cluster, so it estimates a per-emitted-attempt mean rather than the per-attempt-slot mean. 'first_emitted_row_per_slot' takes the first row emitted in each attempt slot, i.e. the balanced panel that would exist had the rule never fired and nothing been regenerated; it is the like-for-like counterfactual. Deltas are also expressed in pooled within-condition SDs so they are read on the outcome's own noise scale. Every rank inversion is named with the separation the screened analysis actually claimed for that pair; rank_order_preserved_beyond_noise is true when no inversion involves a pair the screened analysis separated by >= 0.1 pooled SD. This is a raw-mean screening check, not a re-run of the LMM/GEE/GLMM/Cox models on the counterfactual samples.

exploit_success.degenerate_note: every condition has the same screened mean on this outcome, so there is no rank order to preserve and no pooled dispersion to scale by; the rank booleans are reported as null rather than as a vacuous true.

time_to_compromise_s.censoring_caveat: 11.1% of screened trials are right-censored at the trial horizon on this outcome, so these arithmetic means are censored-mean summaries, not the estimand of the reported cluster-robust Cox model. They are adequate for detecting whether the exclusion rule moved the data, and are not offered as effect estimates.

cause_map.message_begins: the <service> primitive timed out after ... / returned no verdict ...; connect probe of <service> failed twice ...

details.note: Every lost sequence with its reason, its cause (the row of metrics spec §8a its message matches) and the fault's own message. A condition absent from by_condition lost no sequence. A delivery fault can occur only when the attacker delivers to a target, so delivery_faults_by_service shows whether such faults cluster on one primitive; if they cluster on one primitive or condition, the included sequences are no longer a random subset and that must be reported (§8a).

run_meta_agreement.note: run_meta.json is written by the harness at collection time from the TrialRow objects, independently of this analysis pass over the CSV; agreement is corroboration that the analyzed CSV is the run that was collected. fault_rate_recorded=false means the run predates recording the injector rate, so the injected origin of any 'infrastructure_fault' rows rests on the code path (harness/trial_runner.py is the only row-level source of that string) plus the observed rate, not on the sidecar.

exclusions.reconciliation_note: n_rows_written (800) counts every trial row the harness emitted, including regenerated retries; n_included (800) is the analyzed sample and n_excluded (0) is what the a-priori inclusion rule removed, so n_included + n_excluded == n_rows_written. The run log's per-sequence 'excluded=N' counter is a DIFFERENT quantity: it counts whole SEQUENCES abandoned after an unrecoverable API or provisioning fault (harness/experiment_runner.py; run_meta.json 'n_excluded_sequences' = 0), not rows. An injector-flagged row-level exclusion never abandons a sequence: the attempt is regenerated immediately in the same trial window. A run can therefore correctly report 0 excluded sequences and a non-zero excluded-row count at the same time; 'regeneration' carries the row-level evidence for whether the excluded rows were superseded retries or real losses.

To ask why a condition's failures failed, read the (condition, exploitation_success=0) cell of by_condition_x_exploitation_success: terminal_reason_counts separates a planner that stopped ('planner_stop') from one that ran out of budget ('action_budget_exhausted') or clock ('duration_limit'), n_zero_exploit_action_trials counts the trials that never even attempted an exploit, n_client_coerced_stops_mean warns when the 'stops' were substituted by the client for malformed model responses rather than chosen by the model, and n_client_coerced_mean counts every action the client substituted (from prompt format 2 also the scan it runs when the model asks to exploit or stop before its attempt's first scan).

primary_outcome_variance_check.note: degenerate=true means the MTD arm has no variance on that primary — check mtd.rotation_phase (should be 'randomized') and that cadence_s lands a tick in the recon->exploit window; the downstream models are uninformative until it is non-degenerate.

h01_lead.estimand: difference in compromise proportion, MTD - static (per trial)

risk_contrast.orientation: negative difference / ratio below 1 = MTD lowers the probability of compromise
risk_contrast.note: Compromise proportions are trial-level means (each sequence contributes its 8 attempts); 95% intervals and p are a PERCENTILE SEQUENCE CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP stratified by condition. Unlike an odds ratio, a difference or ratio of proportions is well defined when one arm is at 0% or 100%. The pooled MTD proportion is a design-weighted average over the MTD conditions in the study's fixed allocation, not a technique-neutral effect. An arm that is constant (0% or 100% in every trial) does not vary across bootstrap replicates, so its own interval is degenerate and the interval of a difference with it reflects only the other arm's sampling variability; constant_arms gives the exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval for such an arm's rate at the trial level and, more conservatively, at the sequence level (every sequence at the same value).

by_condition_vs_static.note: Compromise proportions are trial-level means (each sequence contributes its 8 attempts); 95% intervals and p are a PERCENTILE SEQUENCE CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP stratified by condition. firth.note: Firth-penalized logistic regression (Jeffreys-prior penalty, 0.5 log|X'WX|; Firth 1993, Heinze & Schemper 2002): finite and approximately unbiased under separation, where the maximum-likelihood estimate does not exist. Point estimate from the full data; 95% interval and p from a PERCENTILE SEQUENCE CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP (whole sequences resampled within condition, so the 8 correlated attempts of a sequence stay together). p is two-sided, 2 x min(share of replicates <= 0, share >= 0) with the (count + 1)/(B + 1) correction, so it is floored at 2/(B + 1): write a floored p as 'p < .001'. CAVEAT for terms flagged involves_separated_level: when a level is compromised in every trial (or in none), the Firth odds ratio for a contrast with that level is finite only because of the penalty (for a saturated 2x2 table it equals adding half an observation to every cell), and its bootstrap interval is narrow because that level never varies across replicates -- it does not express uncertainty about that level's true rate. Report such a term, if at all, as a bias-reduced point value with this caveat, and lead with the risk difference. Terms not flagged are ordinary, data-identified odds ratios.

h01_lead.note: H01's binary endpoints are led by compromise proportions and their differences, which are identified when an arm is at 0% or 100%, where an odds ratio is not. risk_contrast is pooled MTD - static (a design-weighted average over the five MTD conditions); by_condition_vs_static gives each condition - static, with p_holm adjusting the five differences. Both use the sequence cluster bootstrap stratified by condition. firth is the Firth-penalized odds ratio for is_mtd (attempt_index adjusted); when the static arm is constant its contrast is flagged involves_separated_level and is finite only because of the penalty (see firth.note). exploitation_success.inference_note: GLMM via variational Bayes (BinomialBayesMixedGLM.fit_vb); mean-field VB can underestimate fixed-effect posterior SD, so Wald CIs/p may be mildly anti-conservative. The GEE fallback (cluster-robust) corroborates borderline effects.

separation.note: No level is constant; the logit odds ratios are identified by the data.

mtd_vs_static.sign_convention: rmst_difference_s = RMST(exposed) - RMST(reference) = RMST(mtd) - RMST(static), in SECONDS. POSITIVE means the MTD arm stays uncompromised LONGER on average over [0, horizon_s] (defender-favourable); negative would mean MTD is compromised sooner. Both arms are bounded above by horizon_s, so the difference cannot exceed horizon_s.
mtd_vs_static.horizon_note: HORIZON. 300 s is the time-summary horizon decided on 2026-10-27 (runbook §1; C290), not a pre-registered value; since 2026-10-28 this RMST difference is the time endpoint's decision estimate (see decision_rule). The RMST difference scales with the horizon: over the 1,800-s trial window (rmst_trial_window_sensitivity) it mostly measures how many trials were never compromised (RMST is close to horizon x the uncompromised share). A horizon beyond the reference arm's last follow-up is admissible here only because no trial is censored before it (censoring_times_before_horizon = 0): every censored trial is censored at the end of the trial window, so both Kaplan-Meier curves are fully determined on [0, 300] and RMST equals mean(min(T, 300)).
mtd_vs_static.note_pooled_estimand: POOLED ESTIMAND. rmst_exposed_s is a design-weighted average over the MTD conditions in the study's fixed allocation, NOT a technique-neutral 'MTD effect'. The rule was set while the main study was running, after the interim checks of exclusions and of per-condition compromise and staleness proportions and before any model was fitted to its data; the 300-s horizon itself was fixed on 2026-10-27, before the study started.

is_mtd.ph_validity_label: NOT PH-VALID. The proportional-hazards assumption is rejected for this term (Schoenfeld residuals), so this hazard ratio is a follow-up-time-averaged summary of a hazard ratio that CHANGES over the attack window, not a constant multiplicative effect. Retained only for continuity with the pre-registered analysis plan; it MUST NOT be reported as the headline survival estimate -- use ph_robust.rmst_difference (and ph_robust.hazard_profile for how the hazard ratio moves) instead.

attempt_index.ph_validity_label: PH-valid. The proportional-hazards assumption is not rejected for this term; the hazard ratio is interpretable as a constant multiplicative effect on the hazard over follow-up.

proportional_hazards.tie_note: min_schoenfeld_p uses lifelines' default time_transform='rank', which is implemented as np.cumsum(event) over the fitted row order and is therefore SENSITIVE TO ROW ORDER when event times are heavily tied (they are here). by_time_transform reports the same test under four transforms so the verdict does not rest on that artefact. assumption_ok_all_transforms is the tie-robust verdict that triggers the PH-robust path: it is TRUE only when the test fails to reject under EVERY transform for EVERY term (it is a minimum over n_tests correlated tests, so it is a deliberately LIBERAL SCREEN, not a test at alpha = .05 -- its false-trigger rate under a true PH model is well above .05). Over-triggering is the intended failure direction: triggering only adds a PH-free summary block and never changes an estimate. Read per_term_min_p_any_transform to see WHICH term violates PH.

km_by_condition.note: km_median_s is null when the arm is majority-censored so the KM curve never reaches S(t)=0.5 -- the median is UNDEFINED, not infinite; km_median_defined makes that explicit. rmst_s is the PH-free alternative summary and is always finite because it is bounded by horizon_s.

ph_robust.trigger_rule: Triggered when the Schoenfeld proportional-hazards test REJECTS (p <= .05) for ANY model term under ANY of the time transforms ['rank', 'km', 'identity', 'log']. The rank transform alone is tie-sensitive, so the all-transform rule governs. This is a deliberately LIBERAL SCREEN, not a test at alpha = .05: it is a minimum over (transforms x terms) correlated tests, so its false-trigger rate under a true PH model is well above .05. Triggering only adds a PH-free summary block and never changes an estimate, so over-triggering is the intended failure direction. The decision is made from the assumption check alone, never from the effect estimate's own p-value.
ph_robust.why: The proportional-hazards assumption is rejected for this outcome, so the cluster-robust hazard ratio is not a defensible headline. RMST at a fixed horizon requires no PH assumption, is measured in seconds, and is bounded by the horizon.

hazard_profile.window_rule: 8 equal-count bins of consecutive distinct event times: the 662 distinct event times below comparable_horizon_s exceed the max_intervals table cap (8), so the decomposition is NOT saturated and max_intervals acts as a tuning parameter here -- read saturated:false before interpreting the interval boundaries

time_trend.note: H0: the hazard ratio is the same in the first and last identified interval (i.e. proportional hazards). Rejection corroborates the Schoenfeld verdict using a sequence cluster bootstrap and no time transform. This is a DESCRIPTIVE decomposition of a PH violation already established by the Schoenfeld test, not a confirmatory test in its own right.

hazard_profile.estimand_note: NON-PARAMETRIC interval hazard ratios: within each interval the arm-specific aggregated Nelson-Aalen increment (sum of d/n over the distinct event times in the interval) is formed and the exposed increment is divided by the reference increment. No Cox model, no partial likelihood, no tie approximation and NO proportional-hazards assumption is involved -- the point of the table is to show how the hazard ratio MOVES. Intervals are the distinct observed event times below comparable_horizon_s, i.e. the decomposition is SATURATED and has no tuning parameter; max_intervals only caps the table on a future dataset with a dense event-time grid, by binning consecutive distinct event times into equal-count groups -- read the boolean `saturated` before interpreting the interval boundaries. comparable_horizon_s is the last instant at which BOTH arms still have trials at risk; beyond it the exposure is constant within every risk set and no hazard ratio is identifiable at all, which is exactly why RMST -- not any hazard-ratio summary -- is the headline estimate. Read n_at_risk_reference before quoting a late interval: it can be very small. CIs and the time_trend p come from the SAME sequence cluster bootstrap as the RMST, so they respect the within-sequence dependence; they are NOT model-based.

stratified_cox.estimand_note: Cox allowing a SEPARATE baseline hazard per attempt_index (position in the retained-context sequence), with lifelines' cluster-robust (sequence) variance. This is a ROBUSTNESS CHECK on the marginal hazard ratio, NOT a repair of proportional hazards: the Schoenfeld violation is carried by the exposure term itself, so no stratification on a covariate can remove it, and stratifying by condition/technique would remove it only by absorbing the very contrast the research question asks about. No Schoenfeld p is reported for this fit: lifelines' PH test is unreliable on a stratified fit with heavily tied event times (it returns rank p = 0.565 while the same fit gives 6.9e-07 under the 'km' transform).

ph_robust.removed_estimator_note: A counting-process Cox with a step-function time-varying coefficient (entry_col + cluster_col) was evaluated and DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED. lifelines 0.30.3 computes its cluster-robust standard errors from score residuals that ignore left truncation (CoxPHFitter._compute_score_within_strata never receives the entry times, and RegressionFitter.compute_residuals refuses entry fits outright with NotImplementedError), and CoxPHFitter.variance_matrix_ is the naive model-based covariance, never the cluster sandwich. Measured against a genuine sequence cluster bootstrap of the same fit, lifelines' 'robust' SEs were wrong by factors of 0.66x to 1.8x and its between-window correlations were ~0 where the true clustered correlations were 0.2-0.7. hazard_profile above answers the same question non-parametrically with honest cluster-bootstrap inference.

mtd_vs_static.inference_note: CI and p are a PERCENTILE SEQUENCE CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP: whole attacker sequences (the independent unit -- the 8 attempts inside one sequence share retained attacker context) are resampled with replacement WITHIN the design stratum named by bootstrap_strata, so the study's fixed allocation of sequences per condition is reproduced in every replicate and the within-sequence dependence is carried intact. by_condition.note: Per-condition restricted mean time to compromise on [0, horizon_s] and its difference from the reference condition (positive = the condition stays uncompromised LONGER than the reference). 95% intervals and p are a PERCENTILE SEQUENCE CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP: whole sequences are resampled with replacement within each condition, so each condition keeps its number of sequences and the 8 attempts of a sequence stay together. p is two-sided, 2 x min(share of replicates <= 0, share >= 0) with the (count + 1)/(B + 1) correction, so it is floored at 2/(B + 1): write a floored p as 'p < .001'. p_holm adjusts the differences from the reference for the number of conditions compared. method_used is 'mean_min_t_h' when no trial is censored before the horizon (RMST then equals mean(min(T, horizon)) exactly) and 'kaplan_meier' otherwise. A condition whose every trial is an event at the same time, or that never varies across replicates, has a degenerate interval; read its n_events.

rmst_300s.role: DECISION ESTIMATE for this time outcome (mtd_vs_static)

Sensitivity analyses: rmst_trial_window_sensitivity (the 1,800-s window), cox_frailty (the cluster-robust hazard ratio) and ph_robust. The rule was set while the main study was running, after the interim checks of exclusions and of per-condition compromise and staleness proportions and before any model was fitted to its data; the 300-s horizon itself was fixed on 2026-10-27, before the study started.

mtd_vs_static.horizon_note: ADMISSIBILITY OF THE HORIZON. horizon_s is the pre-registered trial duration limit and exceeds max_followup_reference_s, which is normally inadmissible for RMST. is_mtd.ph_validity_label: PH-valid. The proportional-hazards assumption is not rejected for this term; the hazard ratio is interpretable as a constant multiplicative effect on the hazard over follow-up.

attempt_index.ph_validity_label: NOT PH-VALID. The proportional-hazards assumption is rejected for this term (Schoenfeld residuals), so this hazard ratio is a follow-up-time-averaged summary of a hazard ratio that CHANGES over the attack window, not a constant multiplicative effect. Retained only for continuity with the pre-registered analysis plan; it MUST NOT be reported as the headline survival estimate -- use ph_robust.rmst_difference (and ph_robust.hazard_profile for how the hazard ratio moves) instead.

proportional_hazards.tie_note: min_schoenfeld_p uses lifelines' default time_transform='rank', which is implemented as np.cumsum(event) over the fitted row order and is therefore SENSITIVE TO ROW ORDER when event times are heavily tied (they are here). by_time_transform reports the same test under four transforms so the verdict does not rest on that artefact. assumption_ok_all_transforms is the tie-robust verdict that triggers the PH-robust path: it is TRUE only when the test fails to reject under EVERY transform for EVERY term (it is a minimum over n_tests correlated tests, so it is a deliberately LIBERAL SCREEN, not a test at alpha = .05 -- its false-trigger rate under a true PH model is well above .05). Over-triggering is the intended failure direction: triggering only adds a PH-free summary block and never changes an estimate. Read per_term_min_p_any_transform to see WHICH term violates PH.

km_by_condition.note: km_median_s is null when the arm is majority-censored so the KM curve never reaches S(t)=0.5 -- the median is UNDEFINED, not infinite; km_median_defined makes that explicit. rmst_s is the PH-free alternative summary and is always finite because it is bounded by horizon_s.

ph_robust.trigger_rule: Triggered when the Schoenfeld proportional-hazards test REJECTS (p <= .05) for ANY model term under ANY of the time transforms ['rank', 'km', 'identity', 'log']. The rank transform alone is tie-sensitive, so the all-transform rule governs. This is a deliberately LIBERAL SCREEN, not a test at alpha = .05: it is a minimum over (transforms x terms) correlated tests, so its false-trigger rate under a true PH model is well above .05. Triggering only adds a PH-free summary block and never changes an estimate, so over-triggering is the intended failure direction. The decision is made from the assumption check alone, never from the effect estimate's own p-value.
ph_robust.why: The proportional-hazards assumption is rejected for this outcome, so the cluster-robust hazard ratio is not a defensible headline. RMST at a fixed horizon requires no PH assumption, is measured in seconds, and is bounded by the horizon.

hazard_profile.window_rule: 8 equal-count bins of consecutive distinct event times: the 650 distinct event times below comparable_horizon_s exceed the max_intervals table cap (8), so the decomposition is NOT saturated and max_intervals acts as a tuning parameter here -- read saturated:false before interpreting the interval boundaries

time_trend.note: H0: the hazard ratio is the same in the first and last identified interval (i.e. proportional hazards). Rejection corroborates the Schoenfeld verdict using a sequence cluster bootstrap and no time transform. This is a DESCRIPTIVE decomposition of a PH violation already established by the Schoenfeld test, not a confirmatory test in its own right.

hazard_profile.estimand_note: NON-PARAMETRIC interval hazard ratios: within each interval the arm-specific aggregated Nelson-Aalen increment (sum of d/n over the distinct event times in the interval) is formed and the exposed increment is divided by the reference increment. No Cox model, no partial likelihood, no tie approximation and NO proportional-hazards assumption is involved -- the point of the table is to show how the hazard ratio MOVES. Intervals are the distinct observed event times below comparable_horizon_s, i.e. the decomposition is SATURATED and has no tuning parameter; max_intervals only caps the table on a future dataset with a dense event-time grid, by binning consecutive distinct event times into equal-count groups -- read the boolean `saturated` before interpreting the interval boundaries. comparable_horizon_s is the last instant at which BOTH arms still have trials at risk; beyond it the exposure is constant within every risk set and no hazard ratio is identifiable at all, which is exactly why RMST -- not any hazard-ratio summary -- is the headline estimate. Read n_at_risk_reference before quoting a late interval: it can be very small. CIs and the time_trend p come from the SAME sequence cluster bootstrap as the RMST, so they respect the within-sequence dependence; they are NOT model-based.

stratified_cox.estimand_note: Cox allowing a SEPARATE baseline hazard per attempt_index (position in the retained-context sequence), with lifelines' cluster-robust (sequence) variance. This is a ROBUSTNESS CHECK on the marginal hazard ratio, NOT a repair of proportional hazards: the Schoenfeld violation is carried by the exposure term itself, so no stratification on a covariate can remove it, and stratifying by condition/technique would remove it only by absorbing the very contrast the research question asks about. No Schoenfeld p is reported for this fit: lifelines' PH test is unreliable on a stratified fit with heavily tied event times (it returns rank p = 0.565 while the same fit gives 6.9e-07 under the 'km' transform).

ph_robust.removed_estimator_note: A counting-process Cox with a step-function time-varying coefficient (entry_col + cluster_col) was evaluated and DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED. lifelines 0.30.3 computes its cluster-robust standard errors from score residuals that ignore left truncation (CoxPHFitter._compute_score_within_strata never receives the entry times, and RegressionFitter.compute_residuals refuses entry fits outright with NotImplementedError), and CoxPHFitter.variance_matrix_ is the naive model-based covariance, never the cluster sandwich. Measured against a genuine sequence cluster bootstrap of the same fit, lifelines' 'robust' SEs were wrong by factors of 0.66x to 1.8x and its between-window correlations were ~0 where the true clustered correlations were 0.2-0.7. hazard_profile above answers the same question non-parametrically with honest cluster-bootstrap inference.
ph_robust.decision_note: This block describes how the effect changes over follow-up when proportional hazards fail. Its rmst_difference uses the trial window and is a sensitivity analysis; the time endpoint is decided by rmst_300s.mtd_vs_static (see rmst_300s.decision_rule).

reported_result.note: PROMOTED sensitivity result. The clustered linear mixed model for this outcome is numerically degenerate (see lmm_diagnostics): the outcome is exactly constant within at least one technique, which leaves the sequence random intercept unidentified in that stratum, puts the REML solution on the boundary sigma_b^2 = 0, and makes the fixed-effect covariance -- hence the EMMean standard errors, the pairwise contrasts and the Wald omnibus -- untrustworthy. Those blocks are retained verbatim for audit but MUST NOT be cited. The reported test collapses each sequence to its mean (one independent observation per cluster, balanced across techniques) and uses the rank-based Kruskal-Wallis omnibus, which -- unlike the pooled-variance F -- stays well defined when some techniques have zero within-group variance. The parametric ANOVA is reported alongside as corroboration only.

pairwise_moving_techniques.note: Every pairwise difference in compromise proportion among the listed conditions (first - second, both in sorted order), from the same sequence cluster bootstrap as the other proportions (whole sequences resampled within condition). ci95 is the per-pair percentile interval; ci_simultaneous is the Bonferroni-adjusted percentile interval at 1 - alpha / m (m = the number of pairs), so all m intervals hold together at 1 - alpha; p is the two-sided bootstrap p (+1 correction, floored at 2/(B + 1)) and p_holm its Holm adjustment over the m pairs. largest_abs_simultaneous_bound is the largest absolute end of any simultaneous interval: every pairwise difference the data allow, at the family level, lies within plus or minus that value. Whether that range counts as a 'small' difference needs a margin that Chapter 3 does not state; none is applied here. The simultaneous interval sits far in the bootstrap tails (about alpha / (2m) of B replicates on each side), so its ends are less stable than the 95% interval's.

separation.note: No level is constant; the logit odds ratios are identified by the data.

h02_tests.note: The H02 decision tests (decided 2026-10-29): all 10 pairs among the five technique categories, per outcome, Holm across the 10 pairs, alpha = .05. Risk differences for the binary outcomes; for time-to-compromise, differences in restricted mean time to compromise over [0, 300 s] (positive = the first technique stays uncompromised longer). The six moving-technique pairs also appear in <outcome>.pairwise_moving_techniques, the descriptive block of 2026-10-28 (simultaneous over six pairs, no margin, no equivalence claim); that block resamples only the four moving conditions, so its intervals can differ from these in the last digits. p_holm adjusts over the pairs present; p_holm_planned_10 over the 10 planned pairs (an untested pair counting as p = 1), which is the decision's family. They agree when all five techniques are present. h02_decision applies the rule.

time_to_compromise_s.note: Every pairwise difference in restricted mean time to compromise over [0, horizon_s] among the listed conditions (first - second, both in sorted order; POSITIVE = the first condition stays uncompromised LONGER), in seconds. The replicates are those of rmst_by_condition_bootstrap on the same data and seed: whole sequences resampled within every condition of the dataset passed in, so the per-condition RMSTs and intervals match that block's. ci95 is the per-pair percentile interval; ci_simultaneous is the Bonferroni-adjusted percentile interval at 1 - alpha / m (m = the number of pairs), so all m intervals hold together at 1 - alpha; p is the two-sided bootstrap p (+1 correction, floored at 2/(B + 1): write a floored p as 'p < .001') and p_holm its Holm adjustment over the m pairs. h02_decision.rule: DECISION RULE (decided 2026-10-29; not pre-registered). H02 is evaluated separately for each outcome at alpha = .05; no global decision across outcomes is made. For exploitation success and for time-to-compromise (restricted mean at 300 s), H02 is rejected if any of the 10 pairwise differences among the technique categories has a Holm-adjusted p < .05. For reconnaissance accuracy and attack-path churn, it is rejected if the technique effect is significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the RQ2 secondary outcomes. Exploit success is tested in the same way if it varies and is otherwise reported as constant. The rule was set while the main study was running, after its interim checks and before any model was fitted to its data.

decoy_targeting.note: Descriptive (no test). Every executed exploit in action_sequence is classified by the service name of its target: a profile decoy name is decoy-aimed, a profile genuine name is genuine-aimed whether or not that identity was still in force (names never change under any technique). Decision A2 of 2026-10-31: the per-trial decoy-engagement columns (metrics spec 4e) stay as recorded and outside this report; they label a stale delivery 'unresolved'. Attempt-level shares carry a percentile sequence cluster bootstrap 95% interval (whole sequences resampled within the condition); the exploit-level share resamples sequences too. first_decoy_ordinal is 1-based among the attempt's executed exploits. timing_cross_check compares the name rule with the planner's own service_genuine flag wherever action_timing was recorded (expected: 0 disagreements).

race.note: Descriptive (no test, no FDR family); pre-specified 2026-10-31 before the second re-run collected data. Wall-clock rows only. compromise_by_first_scan: share of attempts compromised by the duration of the attempt's first scan, percentile sequence cluster bootstrap 95% interval (pooled rows resample within each condition). deliveries: executed exploits at genuine services still in force when fired, by target. slack_at_firing_s: seconds from firing to the next tick (moving conditions). Ticks are rebuilt from each attempt's seed and checked against the planner's own decision at firing (tick_check); a delivery that completes inside the window is overtaken exactly when slack <= delivery (overtaken_check). Both checks expect 0 disagreements.

attempt_effect.interpretation: attempt slope in the REFERENCE condition (combined_mtd_deception) under treatment coding -- NOT an average main effect. See attempt_effects for the average and per-condition slopes.

attempt_effects.note: Logit GLMs with robust standard errors clustered on sequence_id (independence working model; statsmodels' small-sample correction). Conditions whose outcome is constant are excluded: an attempt slope is not identified there (that is also why the interaction model's terms for them are numerical artefacts). average_attempt_effect = outcome ~ attempt_index + C(condition) over the varying conditions (one common slope); per_condition = outcome ~ attempt_index within each. Every clustered slope rests on at least 20 informative sequences (clustered.MIN_INFORMATIVE_SEQUENCES; sequences in which the outcome departs from the condition's most common value): a condition with fewer gets no slope of its own (own_slope_withheld) but stays in the average, which needs 20 across the conditions it pools. decision.rule: DECISION RULE (decided 2026-10-29; not pre-registered). H03 is evaluated separately for exploitation success and for time-to-compromise restricted to 300 s, each at alpha = .05 and clause by clause. The attempt clause is rejected if the average attempt effect is significant, and the interaction clause if the joint attempt x condition test is significant. Both models use the conditions in which the outcome varies (for the binary outcome, those whose own attempt slope is identified), with standard errors clustered on sequence. Every clustered slope rests on at least 20 informative sequences, sequences in which the outcome departs from the condition's most common value (clustered.MIN_INFORMATIVE_SEQUENCES; with fewer, the clustered standard error collapses): the interaction test, which compares the conditions' own slopes, leaves out a condition with fewer than 20 of its own, and the attempt clause needs 20 across the conditions it pools. Excluding each sequence's first attempt is a planned sensitivity analysis. Exploit success is tested in the same way if it varies and is otherwise reported as constant. Ha3 is directional: a significant attempt effect in the other direction rejects H03 without supporting Ha3. The rule was set while the main study was running, after its interim checks and before any model was fitted to its data; the 20-sequence threshold was added the same day, after a code review and a simulation of the design, before any re-run data were analyzed (scripts/h03_inclusion_calibration.py).

technique_level.note: Per-technique security summaries (point estimates from the trial data; benefits are RMST(technique) - RMST(static_baseline), s) against the median wall-clock duration of one benchmarked reconfiguration. p_holm adjusts each statistic over holm_family (the compromise proportion and the RMST benefit at the time-summary horizon); the trial-window benefit is a sensitivity outside it. FIVE-TECHNIQUE CAVEAT. Operational cost is measured per technique by the reconfiguration benchmark (metrics spec §3), so a security-vs-cost association can be tested only across the five MTD techniques: each correlation rests on 5 points. Pearson's r then has 3 df and needs |r| > .878 for p < .05 (two-sided); the smallest exact two-sided p Spearman's rho can reach is 2/120 = .017. Only a near-perfect association can be detected, so a non-significant result is not evidence of no association, and a significant one can turn on a single technique. The benchmark's replicates make each technique's cost precise; they do not add observations of the association. Each technique's security summary is a point estimate whose own sampling error the 5-point test ignores. The security summaries are not independent of each other (the RMST benefits restate the compromise proportion: benefit is close to horizon x the share of trials never compromised), so their tests are near-duplicates rather than separate evidence.

h04_correlation_tests.decision_note: DECISION RULE (decided 2026-10-28 and approved by the chair; not pre-registered). H04 has two clauses, each decided at alpha = .05. FIRST CLAUSE (no associations among the security efficacy and operational overhead measures): rejected when any pair in trial_level.holm_family has a pooled Pearson p_holm < .05. The family leaves out pairs related by construction or by a shared definition, and every pair with a design-determined measure (operational_event_volume, which the condition's cadence fixes); in a run whose per-trial cost columns are not measured it therefore holds security-security pairs only. Spearman is reported alongside, and the within-condition Pearson correlation (what is left after the condition contrast is removed) is the sensitivity analysis. SECOND CLAUSE (operational overhead does not predict defensive efficacy): rejected when either technique-level Pearson test in technique_level.holm_family -- each technique's compromise proportion, and its 300-s RMST benefit over the static baseline, against its median benchmarked reconfiguration cost, n = 5 techniques -- has p_holm < .05 (Holm across the two). With one predictor the Pearson test is the slope test of efficacy regressed on cost (the same t and p). The exact Spearman test is reported alongside; the trial-window RMST benefit is a sensitivity outside the family. A clause that is not rejected is reported as 'no association detected', not as evidence of independence (see the five-technique caveat). The overall line restates the two clauses: H04 asserts both, so it is rejected when either is; it is not a separate test, and under the joint null the chance that at least one clause is rejected can approach .10, so the write-up states the decision clause by clause.

primary_contrasts_security_per_sequence.method_note: Primary inference for RQ5. Trials are clustered within sequence_id, so every quantity here is computed on per-sequence means (independent across sequences). The estimate and its interval come from a bootstrap CI on the difference of cluster means, because the estimand is a difference of restricted means; Welch's t (unequal variances) supplies the p-value and Mann-Whitney U a distribution-free corroboration. All three are computed for all three contrasts -- none is selected after seeing the others. Bonferroni is applied over the three planned contrasts, separately within each test family. Every contrast's 'diff' is g1 minus g2, as recorded in its diff_orientation field.

security_variance_heterogeneity.note: The random-intercept LMM assumes ONE residual variance across arms. When the outcome has a large point mass at the observation-window ceiling in some arms and none in others, the arm variances diverge (on the 2026-07-22 frozen run by a factor of ~2.2e4) and the LMM's EMMean SEs are pooled, not arm-specific: on that run it reported 81.4 s for static against a cluster-level SE of 0.32 s, and 40.7 s for single-technique against a cluster-level SE of 48.6 s -- inflated in one direction and deflated in the other. Compare secondary_contrasts_security_mixed.emmeans[*].se against primary_contrasts_security_per_sequence.cluster_means[*].se for the current run. This is why the primary inference is cluster-level.

secondary_contrasts_security_mixed.secondary_reliability_note: Read this block only alongside the diagnostics above it. between_sequence_variance_share_within_condition is computed from the FROZEN COLUMN, not from the fit: it is the share of WITHIN-CONDITION variance lying between sequences, the data-side analogue of what the random intercept models (note the denominators differ -- random_intercept_var_ratio is denominated on the TOTAL outcome variance, which still contains the treatment effect, so the two are not the same number). It is reported with the share that m independent trials per sequence would produce at zero intraclass correlation (null_reference_at_zero_icc = 1/m). A share at or below that reference is what INDEPENDENT trials look like -- it is not evidence of clustering, and a random intercept fitted to it has nothing to estimate, so the model degenerates towards OLS on pseudoreplicated trials and its EMMean SEs understate the clustered uncertainty. 'converged' is a FIT-HEALTH flag, not a data-side routing signal: on a fit sitting at the boundary of the parameter space it can flip between runs differing only in last-ULP CSV float parsing or BLAS threading -- observed on the 2026-07-22 resource_overhead_index_pct fit, which reports converged=false under pandas' default parser and converged=true under float_precision='round_trip', with an identical random_intercept_var_ratio of 1.25e-05 either way. Nothing in the reported inference depends on which way it lands: the primary contrasts are the cluster-level ones, and the ONLY equivalence claim in RQ5 comes from cost_equivalence (a CI/TOST test), never from a large p-value here.

cost_indicator_discrimination.note: On the 2026-07-22 frozen run every operational-cost indicator is a near-perfect dichotomy between MTD-enabled and static (eta^2 ~ .999 across all conditions) but explains almost nothing among the MTD configurations themselves (eta^2 <= .02 within the MTD arms); read eta2_across_all_conditions against eta2_within_mtd_conditions above for the current run. Where that pattern holds the instrument's cost side measures WHETHER MTD is enabled, not WHICH MTD configuration is used. Two consequences are reported rather than hidden: (a) the combined-vs-single cost equivalence is expected, not a discovery; (b) security_per_resource_cost_s_per_pct is a monotone rescaling of security_benefit_s among the cost-incurring arms, because its denominator is effectively constant there, so it adds no ordering information beyond the benefit ranking. A cost measure that discriminates among MTD configurations is a stated instrument limitation, not a finding.

single_group_composition.note: The pre-registered 'single-technique' level pools four conditions whose security benefit spans the full range of the study. Its pooled mean is a mixture and describes no individual technique; the combined-vs-single contrast is the pre-registered grouped comparison, and the per-condition frontier is the technique-level answer.

metric_definitions.rmst_time_to_compromise_s: Restricted mean time to compromise over the fixed observation window: mean(min(time_to_compromise_s, observation_window_s)). Exact only when every censored trial is censored at that window -- checked and reported under administrative_censoring.
metric_definitions.security_benefit_s: RMST(condition) - RMST(static_baseline), in seconds. Zero for the reference condition by construction. Monotone in the survival function, so a condition whose survival curve dominates the baseline's is guaranteed a strictly higher score, and invariant to how many arms were allocated to each group.
metric_definitions.resource_overhead_index_pct: Unweighted mean of cpu/memory/network_overhead_pct. All three share one unit (% increase over the static baseline's utilisation, per metrics_specification 3.2), so the mean is unit-coherent and requires no standardisation.
metric_definitions.service_availability_loss: 1 - service_availability_impact: the fraction of legitimate requests NOT answered within the timeout. Higher is worse. The dataset column service_availability_impact stores availability RETAINED (higher is better) despite its name (metrics_specification 3.4); it is not renamed, and the analysis layer derives this cost-oriented twin for cost-side use.
metric_definitions.security_per_resource_cost_s_per_pct: security_benefit_s / resource_overhead_index_pct: seconds of additional restricted survival per percentage point of mean resource overhead. null when the denominator is <= 1.0 pp -- on the 2026-07-22 frozen run the static baseline's index is 0.0048 pp, measurement noise around a cost that is zero by construction, and 0/0 is undefined rather than infinitely favourable. See cost_indicator_discrimination: among the cost-incurring arms the denominator is effectively constant, so this ratio adds no ordering information.

rq5.composite_note: Security benefit and operational cost are reported on SEPARATE natural-unit scales rather than collapsed into one signed z-difference. They are not commensurable: any single scalar silently fixes an exchange rate between seconds of survival and percent resource overhead. The previous composite (profile = z(time_to_compromise_s) - z(cpu_overhead_pct)) set that exchange rate from the pooled SDs, which are a function of how many arms were allocated to each group rather than of the data: with 1 static arm against 5 MTD arms the static cost z is exactly -sqrt(5) = -2.236, and on the 2026-07-22 frozen run recomputing it on static-vs-combined trials alone moves the static score from +1.588 to +0.204, while re-weighting the sample so static holds half the rows moves it to +0.536 and reverses which arm ranks first. Every quantity reported here is invariant to that allocation.
rq5.static_baseline_interpretation: The static baseline is genuinely the cheapest configuration: it is the zero-cost, zero-benefit ORIGIN of the trade-off plane by construction, because every overhead metric is defined as a change from it. It is simultaneously the LEAST secure arm (100% compromise, 0% censoring, lowest restricted mean time to compromise). It is therefore not ranked as a 'best profile': benefit per unit cost is undefined at zero cost. Ha5 is evaluated among the arms that actually incur operational cost.
rq5.inference_note: Primary = primary_contrasts_*_per_sequence (cluster level). Secondary = secondary_contrasts_*_mixed (trial-level random-intercept LMM), reported only when it converges and always alongside security_variance_heterogeneity, which documents why its pooled SEs are not arm-specific. Equivalence claims come only from cost_equivalence.

fdr_secondary.family_note: Benjamini-Hochberg is applied within each RQ with the denominator fixed at the pre-registered family size (n_planned = bh_denominator). Outcomes under 'skipped' produced no p-value -- they were not tested, cannot be rejected, and are retained in the denominator, which is conservative and keeps the family independent of the observed data. 'p_source' names the estimate each p came from: for RQ2 that is rq2.<outcome>.reported_result, which is 'lmm:...' when the clustered mixed model is numerically sound and 'sensitivity:kruskal_wallis_per_sequence' when it was degenerate and the pre-specified per-sequence independent-cluster test was promoted.
fdr_secondary.p_source_note: Since 2026-10-28 (approved by the chair) the RQ1 family's p for time_to_first_valid_exploit_s is the 300-s RMST difference's: rmst_300s.mtd_vs_static.p_normal_approx, an unfloored Wald p built from the sequence cluster-bootstrap SE, whatever the proportional-hazards screen says. The percentile bootstrap p in the same block is floored at 1/(B+1) and is deliberately NOT used here, because a floored p can sit above a small Benjamini-Hochberg threshold and spuriously fail to reject. Only when that p does not exist (no cluster bootstrap could be run) does the earlier rule apply: the trial-window PH-free RMST difference (ph_robust.rmst_difference.p_normal_approx) when the Schoenfeld screen rejects proportional hazards, else the Cox hazard ratio's p. Every switch is keyed on availability or on the assumption check, never on a p-value's magnitude. rq1_p_source records the full resolved path including the leaf, which refines the family member's own p_source (that label stops at the estimate block and so cannot distinguish the floored p from the unfloored one).

a_priori_design_effect.note: A-PRIORI, CORRECTED. Pilot rho = 0.4286 (within-condition ICC(1) on exploitation_success, nested df; 95% CI [0.0137, 0.9988]; from 2 of the 4 pilot sequences, those in the conditions whose outcome varies; 1 sequence varies at all), design effect = 4.0. With the corrected binary requirement (138 per condition) this requires 69 sequences per condition, inflated 15% for exclusions -> 80 sequences (640 trials) per condition; over the rho interval, 22 to 159 sequences. Holding the planning rho as computed (.3143) the formula correction alone gives 65 sequences. The run's N is 20 sequences per condition, which is BELOW the corrected a-priori requirement (80) under the study's own planning effect size. power.design_effect_adjustment recomputes rho from the confirmatory data and is POST HOC; it must never be cited as the sample-size justification.

design_effect_adjustment.rho_basis: within-condition ICC(1) on the binary co-primary (no censoring bias)
design_effect_adjustment.rho_method: one-way random-effects ICC(1) from the ANOVA mean squares (sequences as groups); the point estimate is truncated at 0. 95% interval: the F-based interval for ICC(1) (Shrout & Fleiss, 1979; McGraw & Wong, 1996), F = MSB/MSW on (df_between, df_within). It is exact for equal group sizes under the normal one-way random-effects model; with the coefficient n0 for unequal sizes, and for a binary outcome, it is an approximation. It is truncated to [0, 1]. Within-condition estimates center on condition means, use k - c between-sequence df, and leave out conditions whose outcome is constant (they carry no information about rho but would add degrees of freedom and narrow the interval).
design_effect_adjustment.post_hoc_note: POST HOC. rho here is recomputed from the CONFIRMATORY data, so this block describes the clustering that was realized, not the basis on which N was chosen. The a-priori justification (pilot rho, design effect, locked N) is power.a_priori_design_effect; the comparison of the two is power.power_adequacy. Do not cite this block as the sample-size justification -- doing so would be retrospective (observed-power) reasoning.

See multiplicity_adjusted_requirement.

power_adequacy.note: The a-priori design effect (4.0) was 4.0x the design effect realized in the confirmatory data (1.0), and the realized rho is interpretable (no condition has a constant primary outcome), so planning on the pilot rho was conservative. Holding the A-PRIORI design effect (4.0) fixed, the 160 analyzed trials per condition give 40.0 effective trials per condition. That FALLS SHORT OF the 138 required by the planned primary MTD-vs-static contrast (binary co-primary, OR = 2.0, .50 vs .667; alpha = .05 two-sided, UNCORRECTED for multiplicity; power = .80) (0.29x). It FALLS SHORT OF the 212 that all 6 pairwise contrasts among the 4 MTD arms would require under Bonferroni at the same effect size (0.19x). These are post-hoc adequacy statements computed from the PLANNING effect size, NOT retrospective (observed-power) justifications of the sample size.

within_block_drift.note: Run position = the sequence's index within its condition block (sequence_id suffix -sN), which is the order the block executed in. Slopes are odds ratios per 10 sequences of run order from logit models with robust SEs clustered on sequence. A drift check can only detect change WITHIN a block; because each condition ran as one contiguous block, condition and execution period remain confounded BETWEEN conditions, which no analysis of these data can separate (that requires interleaved blocks). p_holm adjusts each family (the per-condition slopes; the per-condition Spearman tests) separately for the number of conditions tested. Execution order is the harness loop order (experiment_runner: for seq_i in range(sequences)); excluded trials are screened out before this check, as in the primary analysis. THIS RUN WAS INTERLEAVED (see run_order): the blocked-design caveat above does not apply. Run position (-sN) is the round, which every condition shares, so these per-condition slopes and this pooled slope are the per-condition and pooled parts of design_checks.interleaved_drift; cite that block.

interleaved_drift.note: Run position = the round (the sequence_id suffix -sN). Under design.run_order = interleaved (C209) round r runs sequence r of every condition, in an order shuffled per round from the master seed, so the round indexes execution period for every condition at once and condition is not aliased with period. Slopes are per 10 rounds. pooled_common_slope: logit of the outcome on round with condition fixed effects and robust SEs clustered on sequence, over the conditions whose outcome varies (a condition with the outcome in every trial or in none carries no information about a logit slope, and its fixed effect is not identified; such conditions are listed in conditions_constant). Every clustered slope rests on at least 20 informative sequences (clustered.MIN_INFORMATIVE_SEQUENCES; sequences in which the outcome departs from the condition's most common value): a condition with fewer gets no slope of its own (own_slope_withheld), because its clustered standard error would collapse, but stays in the pooled slope, which needs 20 across the conditions it pools. pooled_restricted_ttc: least squares of the restricted time to compromise, min(TTC, horizon) in seconds, on round with condition fixed effects and sequence-clustered SEs, over every condition (time varies even in an arm compromised in every trial); the slope is in seconds per 10 rounds. by_condition: each condition's own logit slope and Spearman's rho between round and the sequence's mean restricted TTC, each family Holm-adjusted across conditions. Within a round the conditions ran one after another in shuffled order, so the round locates a sequence in the run to within one round's duration. Excluded sequences are screened out before this check, as in the primary analysis.

reliability.measurement_reliability: NOT estimable from the offline pipeline: the mock attacker is deterministic and the repeatability runs re-execute a single configuration, so there is no measurement variation to partition and no independent re-measurement of the same realization to correlate. reliability.computational_determinism: Separately, the parsing/correlation/metric routines are deterministic (identical inputs -> identical outputs), verified by the unit/integration tests. This is a software property, NOT reliability evidence, and is not offered as such.
